string.name: settings_description
string.value: Configure Nimbo for your local API workflow.

string.name: language_description
string.value: Language used by the Nimbo interface.

string.name: help_center_description
string.value: Practical, offline guidance for the current Nimbo features.

string.name: help_center_entry_description
string.value: Read step-by-step guides for collections, imports, requests, variables, scripts, Runner, and real-time connections.

string.name: help_start_create_body
string.value: Use New for HTTP, WebSocket, or SSE. Use Import in the title bar for cURL, Postman, OpenAPI, or Swagger files.

string.name: help_start_send_body
string.value: Set the URL, parameters, headers, authentication, and body, then send the request. The response area keeps status, body, headers, cookies, scripts, tests, and timing together.

string.name: help_start_save_body
string.value: Press Ctrl+S to save a request into a collection or folder. Environments and scoped variables let the same request run against different services.

string.name: help_start_local_body
string.value: Requests, collections, environments, and history are stored locally and require no account. Normal backup exports redact Secret values. Use Settings to control history, theme, language, network defaults, exports, and reset.

string.name: help_collection_structure_body
string.value: Collections are top-level groups. Add nested folders for services or modules, then save HTTP, WS, or SSE requests at any level. Expanding and collapsing nodes changes only the view, not stored data.

string.name: help_collection_manage_body
string.value: Use the three-dot menu on a collection or folder to create requests or folders, edit variables, run that subtree, rename, or delete. A request menu can rename, duplicate, or delete it. Destructive actions require confirmation.

string.name: help_collection_save_body
string.value: Ctrl+S updates an already collected request. For an unsaved tab, it opens a location picker and asks for a request name. Double-click a request tab to rename it; the collection tree updates with the saved request.

string.name: help_collection_environment_body
string.value: Select the active environment in the title bar. Development, Staging, and Production are protected defaults; create custom environments from the Environment page. Environment values form the lowest variable layer.

string.name: help_import_curl_body
string.value: Open Import before Settings in the title bar, choose cURL, paste a command, review the highlighted input, and import. Method, URL, headers, authentication, and supported bodies are converted into a new editable request tab.

string.name: help_import_api_body
string.value: Choose API file or drag a JSON file into the import window. Nimbo detects Postman Collection, Postman Environment, OpenAPI 3.0/3.1, and Swagger 2.0, then shows a preview and warnings before applying changes.

string.name: help_import_mapping_body
string.value: Postman folders and requests become collection nodes, root variables become collection variables, and environments remain separate. OpenAPI tags become folders; parameters, security, servers, and stable request-body examples are mapped where supported.

string.name: help_import_failure_body
string.value: Invalid JSON, unknown formats, broken references, or unsupported required structures stop the import before local data changes. Warnings describe skipped optional features. Review imported authentication and variables before sending.

string.name: help_request_compose_body
string.value: Choose an HTTP method and configure Params, Headers, Auth, and Body. JSON editing supports syntax highlighting, pairing, indentation, undo, and variable completion.

string.name: help_request_auth_body
string.value: Choose None, Bearer, Basic, or API Key. API keys can enter a Header or Query parameter. Literal credentials are masked after editing; variable expressions stay visible so their names and completion remain usable.

string.name: help_request_body_body
string.value: Nimbo supports JSON, text, URL-encoded forms, multipart fields and files, and binary file bodies. Only enabled rows are sent.

string.name: help_request_response_body
string.value: View formatted or raw content, search and copy text, download the original body, inspect headers and cookies, preview images and video, and review timing or actionable errors.

string.name: help_request_error_body
string.value: The error view separates the summary, likely cause, suggested checks, request stage, host, timeout, TLS and redirect settings, system code, and technical details. Copy diagnostics when sharing a report; configure missing variables directly from the error.

string.name: help_variable_scope_body
string.value: Environment values provide the base. Collections and nested folders override them as they get closer to the request. A Collection Runner data row has the highest priority for its iteration.

string.name: help_variable_use_body
string.value: Type double braces in URLs, parameters, headers, authentication, JSON or text bodies, form fields, multipart text fields, and WebSocket messages. Use the suggestion list to complete a name.

string.name: help_variable_diagnose_body
string.value: Open Effective variables in HTTP Settings or the Variables tab in WebSocket and SSE. Each value shows its source and override chain. Missing values appear before sending; Configure variables opens the nearest editable scope.

string.name: help_variable_secret_body
string.value: Mark credentials as Secret. Nimbo also masks common token, password, authorization, cookie, and API-key names. Normal exports redact secret values recursively; never publish credentials in examples.

string.name: help_variable_rules_body
string.value: Names are case-sensitive. Disabled variables, empty keys, and empty final values do not satisfy a reference. Script environment writes and JSONPath extraction update only their explicit environment; they never modify collection or folder variables implicitly.

string.name: help_script_pre_body
string.value: Use the guarded nimbo.request and nimbo.environment APIs to adjust the current send. Successful changes apply atomically and do not silently rewrite the saved request.

string.name: help_script_syntax_body
string.value: Scripts use standard JavaScript, including const / let, strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, conditions, loops, functions, template literals, JSON.parse / JSON.stringify, and throw. Every run has an isolated context, so do not rely on globals left by an earlier script.

string.name: help_script_request_api_body
string.value: Available only to Pre-request scripts. method, url, body, and bodyType are readable and writable. headers.get(name) reads by name, headers.set(name, value) adds or replaces, and headers.remove(name) deletes. The method must be supported. Assigning body while its type is none automatically switches it to text.

string.name: help_script_post_body
string.value: Read the response, log diagnostics, and explicitly publish values to the active environment. JSONPath extraction and declarative tests run after the post-response script.

string.name: help_script_response_api_body
string.value: Available only to Post-response scripts and read-only. Read statusCode, statusText, body, contentType, size, duration, and protocol. headers.get(name) is case-insensitive. JSON response bodies are still strings and should be parsed with JSON.parse.

string.name: help_script_environment_body
string.value: nimbo.environment.get(name) reads the active environment and returns undefined when missing. set(name, value) writes a string to the selected environment. If no environment is selected, the key is empty, or the script throws, none of that run's writes apply. Scripts cannot directly modify collection, folder, or Runner variables.

string.name: help_script_console_body
string.value: console.log / info / warn / error append ordered lines to the response Scripts result, joining multiple arguments with spaces. Logging is diagnostic and does not change success. Never log tokens, passwords, or complete authorization headers.

string.name: help_script_completion_body
string.value: The editor highlights JavaScript. Type nimbo., nimbo.request., or nimbo.response. to see stage-appropriate suggestions. Use Arrow keys to choose, Enter or Tab to complete, and Esc to close. After sending, open response Scripts for stage, success/error/timeout/memory-limit state, duration, stack, and console output.

string.name: help_script_order_body
string.value: The fixed order is Pre-request script, effective-variable resolution, network request, Post-response script, JSONPath extraction, then declarative tests. A failed Pre-request script blocks the send. Failed script writes are not partially applied.

string.name: help_script_safety_body
string.value: Every execution uses a fresh local sandbox. Defaults are 500 ms and 8 MB, with a 512 KB stack, 1 MB source, two concurrent scripts, and at most 200 or 64 KB of console lines. Network, files, remote modules, third-party packages, and the full Postman pm.* API are unavailable.

string.name: help_automation_extract_body
string.value: Preview a JSONPath against the latest response, choose an explicit target environment, and control secret marking and overwrite behavior before enabling a rule.

string.name: help_automation_test_body
string.value: Check status codes, response time, headers, and JSONPath values without executing arbitrary code. Every enabled rule produces a deterministic result.

string.name: help_automation_order_body
string.value: Extraction reports invalid JSON, invalid paths, no match, missing target, or conflicts separately. Existing values are preserved unless overwrite is enabled. Tests show expected and actual values and do not mutate the request or environment.

string.name: help_automation_runner_body
string.value: Run a collection or folder sequentially, repeat iterations, stop safely, and optionally provide local CSV or JSON data. Row values are temporary and override scoped variables only for that iteration.

string.name: help_runner_start_body
string.value: Use the run icon on a collection or folder, choose the environment and iteration count, optionally select a data file, review the request count, and start. WS and SSE requests are skipped because a Runner executes finite HTTP requests.

string.name: help_runner_data_body
string.value: CSV uses a unique, non-empty header row and supports quoted fields, escaped quotes, and embedded newlines. JSON must be a non-empty array of flat objects whose values are string, number, boolean, or null.

string.name: help_runner_report_body
string.value: Each request iteration records queued, running, passed, failed, or cancelled state, status code, duration, test totals, message, and details. Filter the list and export the report; data-row contents and secret values are not included.

string.name: help_runner_limits_body
string.value: Data files are limited to 2 MB, 1000 rows, and 100 columns. Runs are sequential, not concurrent. Stop prevents new requests from starting and cancels the active request where possible; completed results remain visible.

string.name: help_realtime_ws_body
string.value: Configure WS or WSS, headers, and authentication; connect, exchange text messages, search or export the timeline, and inspect connection records. Valid JSON messages are pretty-printed and syntax-highlighted automatically.

string.name: help_realtime_sse_body
string.value: Choose an HTTP method, configure headers, authentication, and an optional JSON or text body, then connect to an event-stream endpoint. POST bodies support variable completion. Valid JSON event data is pretty-printed and highlighted; plain text remains unchanged.

string.name: help_realtime_history_body
string.value: Connection summaries enter global history, while WebSocket messages, SSE event bodies, and connection records stay in the current tab memory and are cleared when the tab or app closes.

string.name: help_shortcut_search_body
string.value: Find requests, collections, history, environments, and primary commands without leaving the keyboard.

string.name: help_shortcut_send_body
string.value: Send the active HTTP request from the request editor.

string.name: help_shortcut_save_body
string.value: Update an existing collected request or choose a collection and folder for a new request.

string.name: help_shortcut_editor_body
string.value: Use Ctrl+A to select all, Ctrl+Z to undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y to redo, Tab and Shift+Tab for indentation, arrow keys for suggestions, Enter or Tab to accept, and Esc to close transient search or suggestion UI.

string.name: help_trouble_variable_title
string.value: A variable is missing or has the wrong value

string.name: help_trouble_variable_body
string.value: Open Effective variables, verify exact casing, enabled state, and a non-empty value, then inspect its source and override chain. Configure variables opens the nearest scope. Runner data may override a value only during an iteration.

string.name: help_trouble_network_title
string.value: DNS, connection, TLS, or timeout error

string.name: help_trouble_network_body
string.value: Expand the error details and check the recorded stage and system code. Verify the protocol, host, port, VPN or proxy, service binding, certificate chain, system clock, SSL setting, redirects, and timeout. Copy diagnostics before changing the request.

string.name: help_trouble_import_title
string.value: An import is rejected or incomplete

string.name: help_trouble_import_body
string.value: Confirm the source is valid JSON or a complete cURL command and review preview warnings. OpenAPI YAML is not accepted by the JSON importer. Unsupported optional features are skipped explicitly; required structural errors prevent the entire import.

string.name: help_trouble_restore_title
string.value: Workspace or history was not restored

string.name: help_trouble_restore_body
string.value: Check Restore workspace and Save history in Settings, plus the retention period. Real-time message and event bodies are intentionally memory-only. Reset restores safe defaults and removes local application data, so export a redacted backup first.
